sections.content: How many people are "marine and waterways transport operatives"?

5,510 people

were counted on the census as "marine and waterways transport operatives" in England and Wales in March 2021.

Marine and waterways transport operatives supervise and carry out a variety of deck duties and operate and maintain engines, boilers and mechanical equipment on board ships, boats and other marine vessels.

More men than women had this job

Among people working as "marine and waterways transport operatives" there were more men than women (92.2% compared with 7.8%).

This means "marine and waterways transport operatives" had a similar proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "transport and mobile machine drivers and operatives".

Men made up 92.2% and women made up 7.8% of "marine and waterways transport operatives"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "marine and waterways transport operatives" included:

  • forestry and related workers
  • aerospace engineers
  • IT network professionals

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

People who had this job were generally similar in age to the working population

The occupation of "marine and waterways transport operatives" had a similar age profile compared with the whole working population.

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 55 to 59 years. Of the whole working population 10.4% were aged 55 to 59 years. For people working as "marine and waterways transport operatives", 13.5% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "marine and waterways transport operatives" was 16 to 19 years.

  • groundsmen and greenkeepers
  • metal working production and maintenance fitters
  • forestry and related workers

Select your age group to see the ten most popular occupations for your age

We can look at who worked as "marine and waterways transport operatives" by age group and for men and women at the same time to see how these two factors interact.

Among those aged 50 years and older, we see there is a higher proportion of men with this occupation than women.

The percentage of men and women who are "marine and waterways transport operatives" across age groups

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "marine and waterways transport operatives", 6.6% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had a similar age profile compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work full-time than part-time (88% compared with 12%).

They are also more likely to be an employee (86.6%) than self-employed (13.4%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was the South East. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Cornwall, this is in the region of the South West.
